title: Column marginal of the empirical joint distribution
statement:
Consider $T > 0$ rounds of play between a row player with $M$ actions and a column player with $N$ actions, where in round $t$ the row player uses the mixed strategy $p_t$ over the row actions and the column player uses the mixed strategy $q_t$ over the column actions. Form the empirical joint distribution $\sigma$ assigning to each profile $(i,j)$ the time-averaged probability $\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T} (p_t)_i (q_t)_j$. Then for each column action $j$, the column marginal $\sigma^{\mathrm{col}}_j = \sum_i \sigma_{ij}$ equals the time-average of the column player's weights on $j$,
\[
\sigma^{\mathrm{col}}_j = \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T} (q_t)_j.
\]
hypotheses_covered: row player's mixed strategies p_t over M row actions
column player's mixed strategies q_t over N column actions
replaced:
The column marginal of the empirical joint distribution at action $j$ equals
the time-average of the column player's mixed-strategy weights:
$(1/T)\sum_{t} (q_t)_j$.
